One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 falls to the fallback unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2). Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The report calls the tumour a germ cell tumour without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. A tumour with more than one germ cell component is coded at the mixed germ cell tumour step instead. One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 falls to the fallback unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2). Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). Residual risk, teratoma: glypican-3 stains 20-38% and tissue alpha-fetoprotein 0-27% of teratomas (Siegmund p. 38); nuclear HNF1-beta stains enteric-type teratoma glands in 11/16 (Rougemont p. 26; Table 5, p. 33); Wu Tables 1-2 found glypican-3 in 1/10 and alpha-fetoprotein in 2/10 mature teratomas, weak and in 2-3% of cells. No source reports how often a teratoma expresses both markers of a pair; one that does is coded 9071/3. Residual risk, choriocarcinoma: OCT3/4 negative and glypican-3 positive in 33-100% (Table 1, p. 34; p. 38); each pair needs a second marker the sources report choriocarcinoma rarely or never shows (alpha-fetoprotein, p. 38; nuclear HNF1-beta, Rougemont p. 26). SALL4 is declared and asked by no rule: it marks germ cell lineage, not type (Siegmund p. 36). Choriocarcinoma is not coded from immunohistochemistry (contract §4.2). Fallback 9064/3 per D2.

nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The report calls the tumour a germ cell tumour without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. A tumour with more than one germ cell component is coded at the mixed germ cell tumour step instead. One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 falls to the fallback unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2). Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). Residual risk, teratoma: glypican-3 stains 20-38% and tissue alpha-fetoprotein 0-27% of teratomas (Siegmund p. 38); nuclear HNF1-beta stains enteric-type teratoma glands in 11/16 (Rougemont p. 26; Table 5, p. 33); Wu Tables 1-2 found glypican-3 in 1/10 and alpha-fetoprotein in 2/10 mature teratomas, weak and in 2-3% of cells. No source reports how often a teratoma expresses both markers of a pair; one that does is coded 9071/3. Residual risk, choriocarcinoma: OCT3/4 negative and glypican-3 positive in 33-100% (Table 1, p. 34; p. 38); each pair needs a second marker the sources report choriocarcinoma rarely or never shows (alpha-fetoprotein, p. 38; nuclear HNF1-beta, Rougemont p. 26). SALL4 is declared and asked by no rule: it marks germ cell lineage, not type (Siegmund p. 36). Choriocarcinoma is not coded from immunohistochemistry (contract §4.2). Fallback 9064/3 per D2.

Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30 stains embryonal carcinoma (83-100%) and focally stains 0-50% of seminomas; CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma (Leroy). OCT3/4 marks seminoma and embryonal carcinoma (100% each, p. 37). negative CD117 and SOX17: added to the contract's rule, so a seminoma with focal CD30 is not coded embryonal carcinoma. SOX17 is negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas (Nonaka, p. 37).

No CD30 negative: a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 positive fires this rule (rule 1 requires SOX17 not positive), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma and CD30 focally stains up to half of seminomas (p. 37).

nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The report calls the tumour a germ cell tumour without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. A tumour with more than one germ cell component is coded at the mixed germ cell tumour step instead. One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 falls to the fallback unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2). Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). Residual risk, teratoma: glypican-3 stains 20-38% and tissue alpha-fetoprotein 0-27% of teratomas (Siegmund p. 38); nuclear HNF1-beta stains enteric-type teratoma glands in 11/16 (Rougemont p. 26; Table 5, p. 33); Wu Tables 1-2 found glypican-3 in 1/10 and alpha-fetoprotein in 2/10 mature teratomas, weak and in 2-3% of cells. No source reports how often a teratoma expresses both markers of a pair; one that does is coded 9071/3. Residual risk, choriocarcinoma: OCT3/4 negative and glypican-3 positive in 33-100% (Table 1, p. 34; p. 38); each pair needs a second marker the sources report choriocarcinoma rarely or never shows (alpha-fetoprotein, p. 38; nuclear HNF1-beta, Rougemont p. 26).
